audit_items.proof_trace: The exchange_rate formula uses `self.cash` (not `underlying_balance`), and `flash_loan_withdraw` only decrements `underlying_balance` without touching `cash`, `debt`, `cash_reserve`, or `total_supply` — so borrow leaves exchange_rate invariant. On repay, the principal is returned directly to `underlying_balance` (no `cash` update), and the fee goes to `increase_reserve_only` which adds the fee equally to both `cash` and `cash_reserve`, resulting in zero net change to the exchange_rate numerator. Algebraically, minting with `mint_amount = deposit/exchange_rate` is also exchange-rate-neutral, so no deposit/withdraw combination in the same PTB can yield a profit from flash-loan-induced rate manipulation.
